Dear [Mr Craik](../persons.html#379)
In a day or two you will receive from the [National Society](../others.html#32) a story of mine called [Grisly Grisell](../books.html#228).

It was written for them, but has turned out too historical for their purpose, and as a tale was wanted to be coupled with [‘The Rubies of St Lo’](../books.html#234) I think it will serve the purpose.

Mr [George Macmillan](../persons.html#1946) knows all about the Rubies, which are in the Christmas number of the [Monthly Packet](../others.html#52).

Grisly Grisell is a variation on Sir Gawain’s ‘Loathly Lady’[^1]
[Miss Coleridge](../persons.html#329) agrees to accept £100 between us for the copyright of ‘Strolling Players’.

Really by far the best and most original part is hers.

The idea was mine, but I did not know enough about theatricals to carry it out

Yours truly

C M Yonge

[^1]: The story of Sir Gawain and the Loathly Lady occurs in many versions of which the best known is perhaps Chaucer\'s \'Wife of Bath\'s Tale\'.
